cells.tense: Right now you are the one holding the shape while it is still growing.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Put down the finished thing you keep carrying out of habit. The hours it was taking go back to what's still growing.
cells.core:
Learning by tending is the shape of this. Staying with a thing day after day, hands on, teaches you how it develops, and you can hold the form while it does that without going stiff or snapping it. That's real strength, and right now it's doing what it's for.

The release that comes with finishing is what's free next. When something is done, it can be finished — not a defeat, just the end of the work — and the hours go back to what isn't done. Pick what is genuinely complete and set it aside. Notice what your hands do with the space.
cells.sheetLine: What's finished, you can put down. What isn't, you carry.
cells.verb: Tending what is still growing, and learning from your own hands how form comes
cells.place: Where you bear what has to be borne without breaking or going rigid

cells.tense: You are bracing a future that hasn't asked to be built yet.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Before you plan the next stretch, sit a few minutes with what's actually coming. Just sense it, and let your shoulders answer first.
cells.core:
You carry what has to be carried, and carrying is doing more of the work than it can hold. Anything unfinished gets scaffold thrown around it before its shape shows. That stopped being endurance a while back. It's bracing, and it costs more than the load ever did.

Quieter than planning is the wonder available here. Before you map the next stretch, sit with what's actually coming. Not a solution — just sense it, and let your shoulders answer first. What you feel there is real information about how much fits. What you carry gets lighter when it's what matters, not when the plan is forced through.

cells.tense: You stopped laying hands on what wanted to grow, a while back.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something with no payoff attached — seed, first page, walk with no route. Start it for the beginning itself.
cells.core:
The strength to bear is present and has nothing to do. Hands-on tending has paused. You're standing at the near edge of something already begun, and your hands stay still — not because the strength went, because you're waiting on direction before you move. When it's going well it's simple: you pick a thing up, tend it, watch it change under your hands, and the change teaches you where to go next.

Start something before you know where it goes. Not the big thing, nothing that has to justify itself — a seed, a first page, a walk with no route. Energy from beginning feeds the bearing from below. What grows out of it shows you what you can hold.

cells.tense: You carry it and call the carrying nothing much, while you keep doing it.
cells.act: bear the duty and know when to let go
cells.ask: Name what you're carrying and which pieces are finished. Let one finished piece go — no scene, just stop.
cells.core:
Bearing runs all the time, and it can run well. You stand under weight that would tire others, you don't crack, you don't turn rigid, and your hands stay steady while the thing you're holding develops. Others lean on that steadiness without noticing they lean, because you made the standing look like standing.

What has slipped is your own account of it. You call the weight ordinary and the hours normal, so keeping something upright looks like just how things go. Start with the list: which loads are finished, which still need you. One finished one goes down by your hand, and nothing is lost.
cells.sheetLine: You carry more than you'll say. One finished load can go.
